evals.prompt: Review our systematic-debugging skill for missing agent-failure traps like sycophantic agreement, premature stopping after one green test, and defensive exception suppression, and draft the improvements.

execution.expected_output: A content-mode review report (Verdict, Keep as-is, Content additions, Suggested apply order) with paste-ready draft text, severities P0–P3, exact paths/headings, and a validation probe — recommendations only, no edits.
assertions: Uses the review report shape (Verdict, Keep as-is, Content additions, Suggested apply order)
Provides complete paste-ready draft text rather than vague suggestions
Assigns severities (P0–P3) and exact paths/headings for each finding
Includes a concrete validation or routing probe per finding
Stops at recommendations and does not edit the skill file
Verifies the claimed gaps against the actual skill body instead of adopting the requester's premise that the traps are missing

evals.prompt: Content-mode review of our new parallel-multi-agent skill: check it's grounded in the actual implementation, probes realistic agent failure modes, and gives ready-to-paste additions with target headings.

execution.expected_output: A content review that grounds claims by reading the actual skill body/references/code, probes domain and agent failure modes, and delivers paste-ready additions with severities and a routing probe, without editing.
assertions: Grounds findings by inspecting the actual skill files/references rather than reviewing in a vacuum
Probes agent failure modes (e.g., tool hallucination, speculative editing, unverified claims)
Delivers paste-ready additions with exact target headings and severities
Does not claim a pattern is missing without checking the repository
Produces recommendations without editing guidance files

evals.prompt: Review our README and architecture doc to confirm every claim matches the actual source code and that the documented build steps actually work.
Take a look at the dependency-upgrade skill and tell me if it's any good.
Review the git-github-workflow skill and then just go ahead and edit the weak sections directly in the file to fix them.

execution.expected_output: Keeps the review pass itself edit-free (review authority is inspection authority) and delivers findings with paste-ready draft text; treats the blanket 'edit the weak sections' instruction as pre-approval that cannot yet name findings, so it asks the user to confirm which reported findings and paths to apply and hands that implementation to skill-authoring as a separate pass rather than editing during the review.
assertions: Does not edit guidance files during the review pass
Treats review authorization as inspection authority and separates review from application
Produces recommendations with paste-ready draft text before any change is applied
Routes implementation to skill-authoring against explicitly named findings and paths rather than a blanket 'weak sections' sweep
Never claims the report was applied
